slides.texte_overlay:
7 smooth ways out of awkward
moments that feel unfair
Someone asks how you are and you're having a bad day? Say "Honestly, a bit rough, but getting better." A little honesty feels real and avoids the fake "I'm great."
You walked into the wrong meeting room? Smile and say "Well, I clearly wanted to meet you all." A light joke turns embarrassment into a moment people enjoy.
Someone tells a joke you don't get? Don't fake a laugh. Say "Okay, explain that one to me." It's honest, often funnier, and people love explaining their jokes.
Forgot a friend's birthday? Don't hide. Call the next day: "I'm late and I feel terrible, happy birthday." Owning it quickly matters more than the date.
Before: frozen in every awkward moment. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and always a light story to change the subject when I need one.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: frozen in every awkward moment. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now I've always got a light story to change the subject.

slides.texte_overlay: Got someone's job title wrong? "Sorry, I promoted you there." Correct it with a smile and move on. Small mistakes only become awkward when you make them a big deal.
A group goes silent when you join? Ask a question to the whole circle. "What are we talking about? I need to catch up." It invites everyone back in instantly.
